newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium freezes Mobutu assets at Congo's request.
newsitem.headline: Belgium freezes Mobutu assets at Congo's request.

text.p: Belgium has decided to freeze all the assets owned by former Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko in the country at the request of Zaire's new rulers.

Public prosecutor Jos Colpin told Reuters on Thursday the step had been taken after the prosecutor general of the Democratic Republic of Congo (the former Zaire) asked Belgium to seize money, valuables and personal goods owned by Mobutu.
In connection with allegations of money laundering by Mobutu and relatives linked to the request, Belgian news agency Belga said investigators searched Brussels bank offices.
A Belgian Justice Ministry spokesman had no comment.

Bank Belgolaise, whose offices were searched on Wednesday and Thursday, said in a statement, "Belgolaise and other Belgian banks received requests from the justice authorities to freeze money of a limited number of persons from ex-Zaire. We are not authorised to give details."
Belgolaise has a large African banking network.
Louise Van Heel, spokeswoman for BBL bank, denied media reports the bank's offices had been searched, but said accounts had been frozen at the request of the authorities.

The request to seize the assets of Mobutu and relatives was handed to the Belgian authorities on Saturday by Bizima Karaha, the Congolese Minister of Foreign Affairs, during a stopover in Brussels on a flight from Kinshasa to Washington.
Belga and other media said the actions had been triggered by news earlier this month of the sale for 200 million Belgian francs ($5.5 million) of a mansion near Brussels owned by Mobutu.
The reports said Mobutu was trying to cash in on his holdings in Belgium and export the money to Morocco, where he has found refuge since being ousted by Congo's new leader Laurent Kabila.
Under Belgian law real estate cannot be seized, but bank accounts and cash can be confiscated.
